facts.name: doors we can knock in the days left

answer.question: Based on our pace and what's left, should we ask the client for more doors, or a second pass on the turf we have?
answer.answer:
Ask the client for more doors first — at our current pace we'll run out of first-pass turf, so a second pass would be the fallback, not the first choice.

- Remaining capacity: 1,489.1 average daily doors (last 7 days) × 16 knocking days left ≈ 23,826 doors [table:v_office_pace]
- Untouched doors left in our turf: 10,393 [table:v_precinct_coverage]
- Capacity (≈23,826) is more than double the untouched doors (10,393), so we'll run out of first-pass turf before the program ends [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass]
- We're also slightly behind overall: projected 57,329 doors vs. 60,632 goal, a −3,303 shortfall [table:v_office_pace]

The rule is to ask for more doors first (new turf contacts at the normal first-pass rate) and treat a second pass on not-home doors as the fallback, since second passes contact at roughly half the first-pass rate [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass].

cases.question: Why does the client's daily report show more doors than our dashboard for Oct 12?

answer.question: Why does the client's daily report show more doors than our dashboard for Oct 12?
answer.answer:
The client's daily report shows more doors than our dashboard because the client's sheet counts attempts as submitted before any QC rollback, while our dashboard counts doors with rollbacks removed [doc:counting-doors#why-the-client-s-numbers-differ-from-ours]. On Oct 12 the gap is almost entirely Eastgate's rollback.

- Client report counts: Eastgate 498, Harbor 428, Northside 558 [table:client_daily_report]
- Our dashboard counts: Eastgate 342, Harbor 406, Northside 533 [table:v_daily_doors]
- Eastgate had 142 rolled-back attempts on Oct 12, so its client figure (498) exceeds our doors (342) by 156 — the 142 rollbacks plus 14 repeat attempts [table:v_daily_doors]
- Harbor and Northside had no rollbacks; their smaller gaps are just repeat attempts (Harbor 428 vs 406, Northside 558 vs 533) [table:v_daily_doors]
- The client's report is pulled at end of day and never edited after it is sent, so rollbacks don't change it [doc:client-reporting#daily-report]

SELECT knock_date, office, doors, attempts, rolled_back_attempts FROM v_daily_doors WHERE knock_date = '2026-10-12' ORDER BY office

sources.text: The client daily report counts attempts, pulled at the end of each day before any QC rollback. Our dashboard counts doors with rollbacks removed. The gap on any day is the repeat attempts at the same door plus any attempts that were later rolled back. A normal day shows a gap of a few percent from repeat attempts. A larger gap almost always means a rollback.

The client receives a daily report per office pulled from the canvassing app at the end of each day. It lists attempts (labeled "doors" in the client's sheet) and contacts as submitted, before any QC rollback. We do not edit a daily report after it is sent.

cases.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?

answer.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?
answer.answer:
Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock.

- A shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in that window no longer count as doors or contacts [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]

Flash knocking means recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock.
